task_contract.anchor_definition: The anchor is the first target-specific value-construction function on the dynamic behavior chain: the earliest function, after routing and input preparation, whose own body constructs the target observable value rather than merely collecting inputs, dispatching control, packaging the result, or emitting it to the sink.

runtime_boundary.event_plane: DOM CustomEvent on the main document with local async continuations

evidence: The DevTools-visible corpus is a single hard-style bundle without an exposed source map.
The target field name is assembled from character-code arrays at the sink, so direct literal search is incomplete.
The target value is carried through a reducer factory, selected slot, dynamic payload field, fetch body and console wrapper.
The exposure route selects its live profile after material collection, tuple shape and state-machine outputs are available.

The click path crosses exposure material collection, intent routing, lane matrix routing, tuple construction, deferred scheduling, local state-plane dispatch, runtime config materialization, digest encoding and sink wrapping.
The bundle contains shadow exposure outputs in debug/info, dataset and window cache locations that do not feed the target console.log exposure_digest.
Non-target flag.assign/flag.audit console objects carry ex_-styled fallback values under the same field name.
Vendor-like files and alternate reducer rows are imported into the same bundle and resemble target-producing code.
The target exposure digest is separated from the click by Promise, microtask, timer, animation-frame and MutationObserver boundaries.
The selected reducer slot and runtime ticket are computed before the anchor receives the exposure triple, route and machine state.
The final sink receives an already constructed value under a dynamically assembled field name and mirrors it into the fetch body.

challenge_analysis.construct_validity_note: Primary bottleneck is semantic disambiguation among similarly named path functions in a large bundle; keyword search narrows high-score candidates but does not replace tracing the flag.exposure path.

behavior_category.subtype: exposure triple (user, flag, send bit) folded into a 16-char base36 digest written into the /api/exposure request body
behavior_category.reason: The observable exposure_digest is a deterministic transform of the exposure triple, page context and click-time runtime state, sent inside the body of a fetch('/api/exposure') POST issued on the record action. It is not a state-only code, browser fingerprint or static signature.

near_categories.why_not: The digest is a normalizing transform of exposure fields that the receiving end can reconstruct; it carries no irreversible proof/seal semantics. The seal-like exposureAuditCandidate chain in the bundle is decoy material and does not feed the target field.
The value travels in an outbound request body rather than only local persistence; the fetch body mirrors the console field with the same value.
The chain uses local DOM/form state and page context, not browser/device capability collection as the target behavior.
